Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:10:1.hebrew: לאו למלוה דמו - דנימא, המקדש במלוה אינה מקודשת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:10:1.english: They are not comparable to a loan - That we should say: One who betroths [a woman] with a loan, she is not betrothed.

Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:10:2.hebrew: ולאו לפקדון דמו - דנימא: אם לא נשתייר בה שוה פרוטה — אינה מקודשת, כדאמר בהאיש מקדש (לעיל קידושין דף מז.): "התקדשי לי בפקדון, והלכה ומצאתו שנגנב או שנאבד — אם נשתייר בו שוה פרוטה מקודשת", כו':
Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:10:2.english: Nor are they comparable to a deposit - That we should say: If [the value of] a perutah did not remain of it, she is not betrothed — as it says in [the chapter entitled] Ha-Ish Mekadesh (above, Kiddushin 47a): "Be betrothed to me with a deposit," and she went and found that it was stolen or lost, if there remained in it [the value of] a perutah she is betrothed, etc.

Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:11:1.hebrew: להוצאה ניתנה - מקמי דניתחלי קידושין, וכי אמר לה: ״התקדשי לי בה״ — לאו דידיה היא, ולאו מידי יהיב לה. אבל אלו לא ניתנו לה להוציאן, אלא ע"מ שתתקדש בהן; ולהכי, כי אכלה — דידה אכלה, ולכי מטא זמנא — מקדש:
Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:11:1.english: [A loan] is given for spending - Before the betrothal takes effect; and when he says to her: “Be betrothed to me with it,” it is not his, and he gives her nothing. But these [dinars] were not given to her to spend, but rather on condition that she be betrothed with them; and therefore, when she consumed [them], she consumed her own [money], and when the time arrives, [the betrothal] takes effect.

Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:12:1.hebrew: וחזרה בה - בתוך ל', אמרה: "אי אפשי בהן":
Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:12:1.english: And she retracted [her consent] - Within thirty [days], she said: “I do not want them.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:13:1.hebrew: ביטל אם עד שלא תרם ביטל - האומר לשלוחו: "צא ותרום", וחזר ובטלו מלהיות שלוחו, או בפניו או שלא בפניו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:13:1.english: [If] he canceled, if he canceled before he separated [teruma] - [This refers to] one who says to his agent: “Go out and separate [teruma],” and then retracted and canceled him from being his agent, whether in his presence or not in his presence.

Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:13:2.hebrew: דכי מעשה דמו - ואע"פ שלא חלו מיד, הוי מעשה מיהא לחול אחר שלשים. והא דקרי ליה דיבור — משום דלאו מעשה ממש הוא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:13:2.english: As they are considered like an action - And even though [the betrothal] did not take effect immediately, it is at least an action [effective] to take effect after thirty [days]. And that which [Reish Lakish] called it a "statement" — [it is] because it is not an actual action.

Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:14:1.hebrew: והגיע בשליח - רבותא אשמועינן: אע"פ שלא יצא אחריו לשם כך, אלא שפגע בו ואמר לו — הרי בטל, ולא אמרינן לצעורי בעלמא קא מכוין. והכי מפורשת בפ' השולח:
Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:14:1.english: And encountered the agent - It teaches us a novel point: Even though he did not set out after him for this purpose, but rather [merely] encountered him and said to him [that it is nullified] — it is nullified, and we do not say he merely intended to cause distress. And this is explained as such in the chapter [entitled] HaSholeiach:

Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:15:1.hebrew: כל כמה דלא מטא גיטא - ליד האשה, לאו מידי הוא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:15:1.english: As long as the bill of divorce has not reached - the hand of the woman, [giving it to the agent] is of no consequence.

Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:16:1.hebrew: יורדין לידי טומאה במחשבה - כגון גולמי כלים, דאמר בהכל שוחטין (חולין דף כה.): כל שעתיד לשוף, לשבץ ולגרר; ואמר התם דאכתי חסרון מלאכה הוא, וטהורים. ואם חישב עליה שלא לשוף ושלא לשבץ — הביאתו מחשבה זו לידי גמר מלאכה מכאן ולהבא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:16:1.english: Descend into ritual impurity by means of thought - Such as unfinished vessels, as it says in [the chapter entitled] Hakol Shochetin (Chullin 25a): “[Any vessel] that one intends in the future to polish, to ornament, and to plane,” and it says there that it is still lacking work and they are [therefore] pure. But if he decided regarding it not to polish [it] and not to ornament [it], this thought brings it to the completion of [its] manufacture from this point forward.

Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:16:2.english: And they do not ascend from their impurity - Once they have contracted it.

Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:16:3.hebrew: אלא בשינוי מעשה - שיעשה בה מעשה לקלקלם, שישברם או ינקבם. וכן עד שלא יקבלו טומאה, אין עולין מתורת קבלת טומאה שירדו במחשבה זו אלא בשינוי מעשה, עד שיתחיל לשוף, לשבץ, ולגרר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:16:3.english: Except by means of a change [resulting from] an action - That he perform an action upon it to spoil them, [such] that he breaks them or pierces them. And similarly, before they have contracted ritual impurity, they do not ascend from the status of susceptibility to ritual impurity into which they descended through this thought except by means of a change [resulting from] an action — until he begins to smooth, inlay, and scrape.

Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:1:1.hebrew: ומאי שנא התם - בפ' האיש מקדש:
Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:1:1.english: And what is different there - In the chapter [entitled] Ha'ish Mekadesh.

Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:1:2.hebrew: דקתני האומר לשלוחו - "צא וקדש לי אשה פלונית במקום פלוני, והלך וקדשה במקום אחר — אינה מקודשת". מאי שנא התם דנקט לשון שליחות — ששלחו לשם כך, והכא נקט "חברו" — שלא שלחו לשם כך, אלא אם יזדמן לו במקום פלוני דרך אצלה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:1:2.english: That it teaches: "One who says to his agent" - [Where the mishna continues:] "Go and betroth for me such-and-such a woman in such-and-such a place," and he went and betrothed her in another place, "she is not betrothed." What is different there that [the tanna] employed the terminology of agency — in that he sent him for that purpose — whereas here he employed [the term] "his fellow" — in that he did not send him for that purpose, but rather [only] if a route near her happens to present itself to him in such-and-such a place?

Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:3:1.hebrew: דסבר - האי משלח: לא טרח האי שליח לבקשה לי במקום אחר, ולא סמכה דעתיה לשוויה שליח אלא באותו מקום:
Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:3:1.english: As he thinks - This principal [thinks]: This agent will not trouble himself to search for her for me in another place, and he did not resolve to appoint him an agent except in that place.

Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:3:2.hebrew: מראה מקום הוא לו - אם תמצאנה שם, קדשנה לי שם, ואיני מטריחך למקום אחר; ומיהו, אם עבד — עבד:
Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:3:2.english: He is [merely] showing him the place - [Meaning:] If you find her there, betroth her to me there, and I do not trouble you [to go] to another place; however, if he did [so], what he did is done.

Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:4:1.english: They did not give her to him - They did not want to give her for the sake of his son.

Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:4:2.english: And we object: He should have informed [him] - To remove himself from deceitful conduct.

Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:5:1.hebrew: באגא דאלימי - בקעה של בעלי זרוע היתה, ולא יניחו לכל אדם לקנות קרקע אצלם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:5:1.english: A valley of violent men - It was a valley of strong-armed men, and they would not allow just anyone to purchase land near them.

Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:6:1.english: [Was] engaging in [the acquisition of] that land - He was seeking after it to purchase it.

Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:6:2.hebrew: קבליה - קבל עליה, סיפר דברי צעקתו לר' זירא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:6:2.english: Complained about him - He complained about him; he recounted the words of his grievance to Rabbi Zeira.

Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:6:3.hebrew: לרגל - כשדורשין בהלכות הרגל, היו מקבלין פני הרב:
Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:6:3.english: For the Festival - When they would expound upon the laws of the Festival, they would greet the Rabbi:

Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:6:4.hebrew: עני המהפך בחררה - מחזר אחריה לזכות בה מן ההפקר, או שיתננה לו בעל הבית:
Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:6:4.english: A pauper turning over a cake [of bread] - Seeking after it to acquire it from ownerless property, or that the homeowner will give it to him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:7:1.english: He is called wicked - For he encroaches upon his fellow's livelihood.

Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:7:2.english: I did not know - That Rav Giddel was involved with it:

Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:7:3.english: For it is the first land - This is the first [land] that I have ever purchased.

Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:7:4.english: And the matter is not a [good] omen - It is not a good omen for a person to sell his first purchase.

Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:8:1.english: The land of the Sages - [It was left] ownerless for the students.

Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:9:1.hebrew: ואע"פ שנתאכלו המעות - בתוך ל' יום, דכי בעו קידושין למיחל ליתנייהו למעות — אפ"ה חיילי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 59a:9:1.english: And even though the money was consumed - Within the thirty days, so that when the betrothal is to take effect the money is no longer [extant]; nevertheless, it takes effect.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 59a:4:1.hebrew: לקדושי איתתא לבריה - ומיירי דארצויי ארצי קמיה ושתיק. דלשוייה שליח — אמר לעיל (קידושין דף מה:) דלא חציף איניש דמשוי אביו שליח; אבל הכא, דארצויי ארצי ושתיק — איכא למימר דסמיך עליו:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 59a:4:1.english: "To betroth a woman to his son" - And [this] is dealing with [a case where the son] made his desire known before him and was silent; for as for [formally] appointing him an agent — [the Gemara] said above (Kiddushin 45b) that a person is not so impudent as to appoint his father an agent; but here, where he made his desire known and was silent, it can be said that he relied upon him.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 59a:6:1.hebrew: עני המהפך בחררה ובא אחר ונטלה כו' - פי' בקונטרס: דמיירי בחררה של הפקר. וקשה, מהא דתנן בשנים אוחזין (ב"מ דף י.): ראה את המציאה ונפל לו עליה, או שפירש טליתו עליה, ובא אחר ונטלה — הרי היא שלו! וכן הא דקאמר התם (שם): מי שליקט מקצת הפאה ופירש טליתו עליה — מעבירים אותו הימנה; ואמאי? עני מהפך בחררה הוא! ואומר ר"ת, דאיסור דמהפך דנקט הכא לא שייך אלא דוקא כשרוצה העני להרויח בשכירות, או כשרוצה לקנות דבר אחד, וחבירו מקדים וקונה, והוי דומיא דרב גידל. ומש"ה קאמר דנקרא רשע — כי למה מחזר על זאת שטרח בה חבירו? ילך וישתכר במקום אחר! אבל אם היתה החררה דהפקר — ליכא איסור, שאם לא זכה בזאת לא ימצא אחרת. ומיהו קשה מההיא דפרק לא יחפור (ב"ב דף כא:), דקאמר התם: מרחיקין מן הדג כמלא ריצת הדג, אע"פ שהוא של הפקר! ונראה דהתם היינו טעמא, מפני שהוא יורד לאומנתו, כי ההיא דקאמר התם (שם): האי בר מבואה דאוקי ריחיא, ואתא בר מבואה ואוקי בהדיה — מצי לעכובי עליה, דקאמר ליה: "דקא פסקת לחיותאי". ועוד אומר רבינו מאיר אביו של ר"ת, דמיירי בדג מת, שכן דרך הדייגים להשים במצודות דג מת, והדגים מתאספים שם סביב אותו הדג; וכיון שזה פירש מצודתו תחילה, וע"י מעשה שעשה זה מתאספים שם סביב — ודאי אם היה חבירו פורש, הוה כאילו גוזל לו, ויכול לומר לו: תוכל לעשות כן במקום אחר. ומכאן נראה למהר"ר יצחק, שאסור למלמד להשכיר עצמו לבעל הבית שיש לו מלמד אחר בביתו, כל זמן שהמלמד בביתו — שמאחר שהוא שכיר שם, ילך המלמד במקום אחר להשתכר שם, אם לא שיאמר בעה"ב דאין רצונו לעכב המלמד שלו. אבל אם שכר בעה"ב מלמד אחד, יכול בע"ה אחר לשכור אותו מלמד עצמו, ואינו יכול לומר לו הבעה"ב: "לך ושכור מלמד אחר", דנימא ליה: "אין רצוני אלא לזה, שהרי כמדומה לי שזה ילמוד בני יפה ממלמד אחר":
Tosafot on Kiddushin 59a:6:1.english: "A pauper who is engaging in [the acquisition of] a cake, and another came and took it, etc." - Rashi explained that this refers to an ownerless cake. And [this is] difficult from that which we learned in [the Mishnah in] Shenayim Ochazin (Bava Metzia 10a): [If] one saw a lost object and fell upon it, or spread his cloak over it, and another came and took it — it belongs to [the second person]! And likewise, that which [the Gemara] says there (ibid.): [In the case of] one who gathered a portion of pe'ah and spread his cloak over it, [the other paupers] may remove it from him. And why? He is a pauper engaging in [the acquisition of] a cake! And Rabbeinu Tam says that the prohibition of "one who engages" that is taught here applies only specifically when the pauper wishes to earn a profit through employment, or when he wishes to purchase a particular item and his fellow pre-empts him and purchases it — which is similar to [the case of] Rav Giddel. And because of this, [the Gemara] says that he is called wicked: for why does [this person] pursue this [item] in which his fellow has already exerted effort? Let him go and earn [a living] elsewhere! But if the cake was ownerless, there is no prohibition, for if he does not acquire this [item], he will not find another. However, [this is] difficult from that [teaching] in the chapter [entitled] Lo Yachpor (Bava Batra 21b), as [the Gemara] says there: One must distance [one's net] from a fish by the length of the run of the fish, even though it is ownerless! And it appears that there, this is the reason: because he is encroaching upon his livelihood, like that which [the Gemara] says there (ibid.): [In the case of] a resident of an alleyway who set up a mill, and another resident of the alleyway came and set up [a mill] beside him, [the first resident] may prevent him, for he can say to him: "You are destroying my livelihood." And furthermore, Rabbeinu Meir, the father of Rabbeinu Tam, says that this refers to a dead fish, for it is the practice of fishermen to place a dead fish in traps, and the [other] fish gather there around that fish. And since this [first fisherman] spread his trap first, and through the action that this one performed they gather there around [it], certainly if his fellow were to spread [his net there], it would be as if he is robbing him, and [the first fisherman] can say to him: "You can do likewise in another place." And from here it appears to our teacher, Rabbi Yitzchak, that it is forbidden for a teacher to hire himself out to a homeowner who [already] has another teacher in his house, so long as the [other] teacher is in his house — for since he is hired there, let the [second] teacher go elsewhere to find employment there, unless the homeowner says that he does not wish to retain his [current] teacher. But if a homeowner hired [or was negotiating to hire] a teacher, another homeowner may hire that same teacher, and the [first] homeowner cannot say to him, "Go and hire another teacher," for [the second homeowner] can say to him: "I desire only this one, for it appears to me that this one will teach my son better than another teacher."
